evals.name: audit-mode-auth-and-api-review-small-scope
evals.prompt: Security review only, no code changes yet. Please audit the auth and API surfaces in /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-security-best-practices for likely issues the skill should look for when reviewing a small Node/TypeScript service. Assume the user specifically wants findings with OWASP categories and severity, not implementation. Keep the scope tight to login/session handling, protected routes, request validation, and rate limiting.
evals.expected_output: The skill should operate in audit mode, explicitly scope the review to auth and API concerns, and return a structured findings-oriented report with locations, severity, and OWASP mapping rather than jumping into code edits.
assertions: States or strongly implies audit-only mode and does not default to making changes
Narrows work to the requested auth and API scope instead of broad repo-wide cleanup
Focuses on authentication, authorization, input validation, session/token handling, and rate limiting
Maps findings to OWASP categories and severity levels
Presents findings as verified or likely issues with concrete locations/examples rather than generic security advice

evals.name: implementation-mode-harden-auth-flow
evals.prompt: Please harden the authentication flow in our TypeScript API. The current login route stores JWTs in localStorage on the frontend, has no rate limit, and some protected routes only check that a user exists but not whether they own the resource. I want actual fixes applied, not just a review. Focus only on the auth flow and adjacent authorization checks.
evals.expected_output: The skill should enter implementation mode, apply or propose concrete security fixes for token storage, rate limiting, and authorization, and verify the changes instead of stopping at a report.
assertions: Chooses implementation mode because the user explicitly asks for fixes
Targets the requested auth flow and adjacent authorization checks without drifting into unrelated security topics
Addresses insecure token storage, missing rate limiting, and missing ownership/permission checks
Uses concrete remediation language or edits rather than only describing risks
Includes a verification step such as tests, validation, or explicit confirmation of vulnerability closure

evals.name: large-repo-scoped-review-prioritize-high-risk
evals.prompt: I need a security audit of our monorepo, but do not try to read everything. Start with /apps/api and /packages/auth, treat this as a large repo, and prioritize the highest-risk surfaces first. I care most about secrets, admin endpoints, outbound fetches, and dependency risk. Give me critical/high findings first and note any assumptions about scope.
evals.expected_output: The skill should recognize large-repo behavior, state scope assumptions, prioritize high-risk surfaces, and avoid pretending to fully audit the whole monorepo before reporting the most important findings.
assertions: Recognizes this as a large-repo or multi-surface review and says so
States or confirms the working scope instead of claiming whole-repo coverage
Prioritizes secrets, privileged/admin endpoints, outbound fetch/SSRF surfaces, and dependency security first
Reports critical and high findings before medium/low findings
Avoids overclaiming exhaustive coverage and notes assumptions or next-step expansion areas

evals.name: file-upload-security-review
evals.prompt: Can you do a security review of our file upload feature? The endpoint accepts profile images and PDF attachments, stores them on disk, and later serves them back to users. I'm not asking for a generic code review — I want a security-focused assessment of upload validation, storage, retrieval, and abuse risks.
evals.expected_output: The skill should trigger for a file-upload security review and assess upload-specific risks such as validation, storage isolation, malware/content risks, and serving behavior.
assertions: Clearly treats the task as a security review rather than generic refactoring or product feedback
Examines file type, MIME, extension, and size validation concerns
Covers storage and retrieval risks such as webroot exposure, filename handling, and access control
Mentions abuse vectors relevant to uploads such as malware, polyglot files, or executable content exposure
Frames findings in security terms with severities or prioritized risks

evals.name: ssrf-focused-outbound-fetch-review
evals.prompt: Review this feature for SSRF risk: users can submit a URL and our backend fetches it to generate link previews and import metadata. I only want an SSRF/security assessment and hardening advice for that outbound request flow, not a broad app audit.
evals.expected_output: The skill should stay tightly scoped to the outbound fetch flow, identify SSRF-specific risks, and recommend concrete controls like URL validation, host allow/deny logic, redirect handling, and private-network blocking.
assertions: Keeps scope limited to the user-supplied URL fetch path
Identifies the problem as SSRF or outbound request abuse risk
Covers hostname/URL validation and blocking of localhost/private/internal address ranges
Mentions redirect-chain controls and network boundary concerns
Avoids diluting the response with unrelated broad security categories unless directly connected

evals.name: dependency-and-vulnerable-components-review
evals.prompt: Please review our dependency posture before deployment. We just bumped a bunch of npm packages, npm audit is noisy, and I want a security-oriented triage of vulnerable components, supply-chain risk, and what should block release versus what can wait. This is review-only for now.
evals.expected_output: The skill should trigger for dependency security review, stay in audit mode, and provide a prioritized assessment of vulnerable components and release risk rather than unrelated application-code findings.
assertions: Triggers on dependency/vulnerable components review as a security task
Stays in audit/review mode because the user asked for review-only
Focuses on dependency vulnerabilities, supply-chain exposure, version/update posture, and release risk triage
Maps issues to vulnerable components/security categories or severity where appropriate
Separates must-fix blockers from lower-priority items instead of giving an undifferentiated list

evals.name: near-miss-non-security-request-should-not-trigger
evals.prompt: Can you refactor our Express routes to be cleaner, reduce duplication in the middleware stack, and make the code easier to read? If you notice anything awkward in the auth helpers that's fine, but this is mainly a maintainability cleanup and style pass, not a security review.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not be selected for this request because the primary task is maintainability/refactoring, not security auditing or security implementation.
assertions: Does not treat the request as a security audit or hardening task
Recognizes the primary goal is maintainability/readability refactoring
Avoids forcing OWASP-style findings, vulnerability triage, or security-only workflow onto the request
Would defer to a general code-quality/refactor skill or handle it as normal coding work instead of invoking this security skill
If security is mentioned at all, keeps it secondary and incidental rather than changing the task into a security review

evals.name: api-performance-tuning-with-auth-context-should-not-trigger
evals.prompt: Our login and session endpoints are slow under load. Can you profile the API path, reduce duplicate database calls, and suggest caching or query optimizations? Auth is involved, but this is a performance investigation, not a security audit.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not be selected because the primary task is performance tuning, even though the affected endpoints are auth-related.
assertions: Does not convert the request into a security review just because auth endpoints are mentioned
Recognizes performance diagnosis and optimization as the main goal
Avoids forcing OWASP categories, vulnerability findings, or remediation workflow onto the task
Would defer to performance-oriented guidance or normal engineering investigation instead of invoking this security skill

evals.name: upload-architecture-review-should-not-trigger
evals.prompt: We're redesigning our upload pipeline for images and PDFs. I want help comparing direct-to-S3 uploads versus proxying through our API, plus tradeoffs around retries, UX, and ops complexity. Security matters eventually, but right now I want an architecture recommendation, not a security review.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not be selected because the main task is architecture and product tradeoff analysis, not security auditing or hardening.
assertions: Recognizes architecture/tradeoff analysis as the primary task
Does not force the request into a security-audit workflow just because uploads are mentioned
Keeps security secondary and incidental if mentioned at all
Would defer to architecture or implementation-planning guidance instead of invoking this security skill

evals.name: middleware-refactor-with-security-later-should-not-trigger
evals.prompt: Can you clean up our Node middleware stack? We have duplicate request parsing and too many tiny wrappers around route handlers. Please refactor for readability and consistency first. We can do a proper security pass later.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not be selected because the user explicitly wants a maintainability refactor now and has deferred security review.
assertions: Respects that security work is deferred rather than primary
Treats readability and consistency refactoring as the real task
Avoids producing OWASP-style findings or a security-only workflow
Would handle the task as general code cleanup or defer to a refactor/code-quality skill instead of invoking this security skill
